summary: The live play control seeks replays through the retained-stage time update that docs/recorded-pose-capture.md says may not advance recorded rigid-body sequences, and the observer never checks that the image changed.
failure_scenario: Publish a recording's replay.usdc (reset-stack matrix4d physicsReplay ops), open it in the observer and press play: rt.seek -> ovstage.population.update_from_usd_time is the same path the capture doc avoids with --snapshot-poses. If it does not propagate the sampled body transforms, the timeline and state['seconds'] advance (observe.py:310) while the video stays at the first pose, with no error shown.
evidence: Read observe.py:229-235,310 and recorded-pose-capture.md:3-5 plus commit 707dce6 (snapshot path added for this reason; observer has no equivalent). docs/live-viewer.md tells users to inspect recorded motion with the play control. No GPU or renderer was run, so whether the native update fails for this replay layout is unverified.

summary: max_rotation_degrees is computed with 2*arccos(|dot|) on float32 quaternions, so a body that never rotated can report a spurious rotation of a few hundredths of a degree.
failure_scenario: A stationary or no-drive-control body with a generic orientation (poses.npz float32, identical rows): the normalized dot product rounds to 0.99999994, giving about 0.04 to 0.08 degrees instead of 0. The noise floor sits in the feedback used to compare driven and no-drive runs.
evidence: CPU probe importing engine.measure with pxr stubbed: 2000 random unit float32 quaternions, five identical samples each; 16 of 2000 stationary bodies reported nonzero rotation, worst 0.079 degrees. Assumes ovphysx returns float32 orientations, which was not checked (no worker was run).

summary: A malformed or truncated run.json is silently ignored, so the viewer keeps showing the previous run's prompt, model and status fields with no error.
failure_scenario: run.json is rewritten non-atomically or with invalid JSON while the observer polls: json.loads raises ValueError, the except clause passes, state['run'] and state['field'] keep the old values, and unlike the publication poll (line 152) no state['error'] is set. Requested versus served model evidence can appear current when it is stale.

summary: Replay bounds come only from authored startTimeCode/endTimeCode, which fall back to 0 for animation that has time samples but no stage range.
failure_scenario: Publish a hand-authored animated scene without start/end metadata: wrapper writes start=end=0, observe.py:190 never advances the playhead and seek clamps to 0, so playback shows nothing and no message explains why. Replays from physics_usd.export are unaffected because they author both.
evidence: Read viewer_scene.py:29-33,92-93 and observe.py:177,190. pxr is not installed here, so UsdStage.GetStartTimeCode fallback behavior was not probed.

summary: Quaternion order is consistent end to end: simulate.py stores position then orientation and records xyzw, physics_usd.export reads pose[3:] as x,y,z,w and builds Gf.Quatd(w, xyz). Whether ovphysx itself returns xyzw is unverified.
Body ordering is consistent: simulate.py sorts paths once, rejects membership changes between steps, stores paths with poses, and export/measure zip them with strict=True.

Time codes: replay sets timeCodesPerSecond to the recorded fps and times to seconds*fps; the source sublayer keeps its own rate, so USD layer offsets keep non-body animation in seconds. Fractional float error such as 70.00000000000001 interpolates by about 1e-15 only. Not run (no pxr).

probe_mechanism rig: a parallelogram four-bar (ground 6, crank 2, coupler 6, follower 2). Joint frames and body poses are consistent: crank tip equals bridge origin and bridge end equals follower tip. Only the three moving shapes carry CollisionAPI, pedestals and floor do not, and joints default collision off, so no hidden contact appears. --no-drive only omits the DriveAPI. Checked by arithmetic, not by simulation.

sample_transforms writes a default value in a stronger layer over weaker time samples, which wins in USD value resolution, so the static override replaces the animation. It rejects non-xform animation and instance-proxy animation explicitly. Reasoned from USD resolution rules; not run.

publish.py packs to a temporary name before the final rename and advances current.json by atomic replace; observe.py only accepts all-digit revision stems, so partial packages and torn reads are not picked up.

engine.measure converts displacement with the stage metersPerUnit; that assumes ovphysx reports positions in stage units, which could not be checked without running the worker (probe rig uses 1 m units, so it would not expose a mismatch).
